Forty brothers. The Dragon remembers.
Leave. While we allow it.

Swamp-Drainer. The bosses want a word. A long one.
That's the one who empties the swamp. Don't start nothing.
Sixty of ours in the water because of you.

Reaver-Bane. The black ships remember you.
You've cost us sixty. Someone will collect.
Not here. Not now. Later.

Hive-Burner. Queen is told. Queen isn't pleased.
Many drones gone. You. It was you.
Hive remembers. Hive doesn't forgive.

Hive remembers. Hive doesn't forgive.
Swarm-Breaker. Swarm counts its dead. You're the count.
Kill. Kill. Kill the breaker. Not yet.
The Queen of the South has your smell.

Narko! Narko walks in the light of Okran!
You killed the Holy Lord. There's no prayer long enough for what you are.
Demon. Phoenix's blood is on those hands. I see it.

You killed the Holy Lord. There's no prayer long enough for what you are.
Demon. Phoenix's blood is on those hands. I see it.
Emperor-Killer. Every noble in the Cities wants you skinned.
You killed the Emperor. Do you know how many lords that made happy? Not the ones watching you now.
The Cities will never forgive Tengu's death. Never.

The Cities will never forgive Tengu's death. Never.
You killed Esata. Every Shek alive owes you a death.
Queen-Breaker. Our horns will find you.
Esata's killer. Stand and fight, if you have the spine.

Queen-Breaker. Our horns will find you.
Esata's killer. Stand and fight, if you have the spine.
Prince. Prince gone. You. You.
The Prince's End. Fog weeps. Fog hunts.
Gone. Prince gone. Kill. Kill.
Prince. Prince gone. You. You.
The Prince's End. Fog weeps. Fog hunts.
Gone. Prince gone. Kill. Kill.
Wizard gone. Wizard gone. You.
Bone-man killer. Run. Run.
No more wizard. Only you. Only meat.
Wizard gone. Wizard gone. You.
Bone-man killer. Run. Run.
No more wizard. Only you. Only meat.
The Red Ruin. You put our boss in the ground.
Boss is dead because of you.
Red Ruin. The Sabres want their blood back.
The Red Ruin. You put our boss in the ground.
Boss is dead because of you.
Red Ruin. The Sabres want their blood back.
Kingslayer. The Dust King's dead and the sand is still talking about it.
You killed the King. There's a price on you in every camp.
That's the one. That's the one who did the King.
Kingslayer. The Dust King's dead and the sand is still talking about it.
You killed the King. There's a price on you in every camp.
That's the one. That's the one who did the King.
Dust-Eater. Fewer of them on the roads because of you.
The caravans speak well of you. Rare praise.
Keep at the Dust Bandits. Nobody here will mourn them.
You're the one clearing the starvers off the roads.
The Starver. My sister travels easier now.
Good work out there. Grim, but good.
Sabre-Breaker. You fight the Red Sabres. That's a warrior's work.
The Sabres fear you. The Shek respect that.
Kill more of them. Our scouts will sing of it.
The Skinners are abominations, and you break them.
Skinner's Bane. Walk in the light.
The machines fall to you. Good.
Fog-Cutter. The fog is thinner because of you.
Mongrel owes people like you. More than it says.
You go into the fog and come back.
Eater-Killer. Stay a while. Drinks are on someone.
You thin the eaters. Every village in the west owes you.
Good. Fewer eaters, fewer empty villages.
The Unbeliever. The paladins pray against you. We drink to you.
Fifty of the Holy Nation. That's a good start.
Any enemy of the Nation can rest here.
Samurai-Killer. The nobles fear you. Good.
Fewer samurai, fewer slaves. We remember who did it.
You fight the Cities. We're with you.
The Horn-Breaker. The Nation thanks you for your work against the beasts.
Okran guides your blade against the Shek.
Fifty of the horned ones. Well done.
Slaver's End. Every chain you break counts.
You kill slavers. Sit. You're welcome here.
Word is, the slave roads are quieter.
Hunter of Hunters. The manhunters run from you now.
You turn the hunt. Good. Keep turning it.
Fewer manhunters, fewer sacks over heads.
Narko. That's what they call you in the Nation. Here we call you a friend.
You killed the Phoenix. Sit down. Nobody here pays for your drink.
The Holy Lord is dead and the Nation trembles. Good work, Narko.
You killed Tengu. Do you know how many chains that broke?
Emperor-Killer. The Cities shake. We sing.
Sit. The one who killed Tengu does not stand at our fire.
The Queen of the beasts is dead by your hand.
Queen-Breaker. The Nation will remember you kindly.
Esata's death was a gift to the Nation.
You killed the Fog Prince. Mongrel will never forget it.
The Prince's End. The fog's quieter.
Drink. You killed the Prince. Drink.
The Grand Wizard is dead. The eaters are lost without him.
The Wizard's End. Every village in the west can breathe.
You did what armies didn't. Thank you.
The Red Sabre boss is dead. The Shek honour that.
The Red Ruin. Sit with us.
The Sabres are broken. A good day's work.
You killed the Dust King. The roads are safer. The Guild says thank you, in its way.
Kingslayer. The bounty was well earned.
A bandit king in the ground. Good.
Careful with that one. Hard hands.
I've heard of you. Not good things, but things.
You have the look of someone who has buried people.
Bonepicker. They say you leave nothing for the scavengers.
Keep your hands where I can see them, Bonepicker.
There goes trouble with a name.
The Long Shadow. In my town.
I heard you'd killed more men than the plague. Looking at you, I believe it.
Don't stare. That's the Long Shadow. People who stare get noticed.
Limb-Taker. Counting arms and legs, are you?
I'd like to keep all of mine, thank you.
I heard you take limbs. I need mine for work.
The Carver. People leave your fights in pieces.
Mind the Carver. They cut what they don't kill.
I saw what you left at the crossroads. Was that you? Of course it was.
That's the one who drops people with bare hands.
The Fist. I've seen the faces you leave.
Mind the hands on that one.
The Breaker. Five hundred people woke up hurting because of you.
Don't start anything near the Breaker.
They say you've knocked down half the wasteland.
You're the one who patches people up on the road. Good.
Field Medic. If I fall over, you'll know what to do.
A medic. Rare enough out here to be worth a nod.
The Bonesetter. People say you've pulled more back from the edge than the clinics.
I owe a friend's leg to someone like you.
Bonesetter. Stay safe. We need people who mend.
Word is, you've been put in the dirt sixty times and got up every one.
Hard to Kill. Some would say hard to learn.
You again. Still breathing. Impressive, or stupid.
The Unburied. Death keeps sending you back. Nobody wants you either, it seems.
I've heard you can't be killed. I'd rather not find out.
Two hundred times down. Still walking. What are you?
The Unfinished. The world keeps taking pieces and you keep walking.
Lost another bit, have you? You're a stubborn sort.
There's less of you every time I hear the story.
What Remains. That's the name, and it fits.
More metal than meat by now, I'd guess.
They keep taking bits of you, and you keep coming back for more.
The Walker. Is there a road you haven't worn down?
You've seen more of this country than most maps.
Back again. Where to this time?
The Labourer. Sixty hours at a machine.
A worker. We could use more of those, fewer of the other kind.
Good hands. Working hands.
Wall-Raiser. Building out there takes nerve. Or stupidity.
You put walls up where nobody else would. Good luck with that.
A builder. The wasteland knocks things down.
Keep an eye on your back. The Quiet Hand is about.
I didn't hear you come in. I suppose that's the point.
Quiet Hand. People wake up with headaches near you.
Red Hands. You've spilled enough blood to fill a well.
There's a smell about you. Old blood.
Wash, sometimes. People talk.
The Long Night. Fifteen hundred dead, people say. I believe it now I've seen you.
Mothers in the Hub scare children with your name.
When you came in the room got colder. That's not a figure of speech.

Your crew killed them all. The Phoenix, Tengu, Esata, the Fog Prince.
Nobody's in charge any more. That's your doing.

Heard of the Headtakers? They go for the leader first.
That crew that kills bosses. Twenty-five chiefs, people say. Bad for the bandit trade.
If you lead a gang, you don't want the Headtakers knowing your name.
The Chiefbreakers. A hundred bosses in the dirt. Every gang out there counts its leaders twice now.
Nobody wants to be in charge of anything while the Chiefbreakers are walking.
They say the bandit bosses pay each other not to be first in line.
Some crew's been taking named heads in. The posters keep coming down.
Bounty Takers, people call them. Three names crossed off, and they're looking for the next.
Whoever cashed those bounties has a reputation now.
The Wanted-Enders. Fifteen named heads. The poster wall's getting bare.
Every name on the board is drinking somewhere else now.
Outlaws sleep badly while the Wanted-Enders are about.
The Grave-Fillers. Eight hundred dead, if you believe it.
There's a crew out there that's killed more than the fog. Don't ask me where they are.
Grave-Fillers. Even the scavengers can't keep up.
You're with the Headtakers, aren't you.
Headtakers in town. The bandits will be nervous tonight.
Your lot goes for the boss first. Smart.
You're the crew clearing the poster wall. Some say thank you. Some say watch your back.
Wanted-Enders. My cousin's village sleeps better because of you.
The board's half empty. That's your doing.
You're the smith people talk about.
The Smith. If my blade breaks, I know who to find.
Your work's turning up all over.
The Armourer. People walk out of fights in your plates.
Good armour's worth more than a good sword. You'd know.
I heard your armour stops what other armour doesn't.
You have the look of someone who has seen a lot of fights.
A veteran. You can tell by how they stand.
Fifty fights and still walking. Not many can say that.
They say you were the last one standing.
Last One Standing. Your friends must be glad you're stubborn.
When everyone else drops, you keep going. I've heard the stories.
The Old Hand. Every scar has a story, and you have a lot of scars.
A hundred and fifty fights. You must be tired.
Old Hand. Don't start anything with that one.
That crew they call the Unbroken. Four hundred fights won between them.
The Unbroken. Knock them down, they get up, they win anyway.
Nobody bets against the Unbroken any more.
